newsitem.title: USA: N.J. Senate cancels hearing on $3 bln bond plan.
newsitem.headline: N.J. Senate cancels hearing on $3 bln bond plan.

text.p: A New Jersey Senate committee on Monday cancelled hearings set for Tuesday on a controversial $3 billion pension obligation bond deal, a state Senator said.
The delay came at the request of Senate Republicans, according to Sen. Robert Littell, R-Sussex, chairman of the Senate Budget and Appropriations Committee.
Littell, who opposes the pension bond plan, said in a telephone interview that supporters of the proposal wanted more time to win the backing of key unions in the state.

The New Jersey Education Assocation, the state's 150,000-member teachers union, has already said it supports the idea, but Littell said several other unions are holding out for more concessions from the state.

Littell also said hearings in the state Assembly originally set for Thursday would likely be postponed, in part because state Assembly members want the Senate to vote before taking up the idea themselves.
A spokeswoman for state Treasurer Brian Clymer, who was scheduled to testify at the Senate hearing, said the administration had not been told when it might be rescheduled.

The bond plan, proposed earlier this year by Gov. Christine Whitman, is intended to eliminate a $4.2 billion unfunded liability in the state's pension system. The bonds, in combination with a move to tap $1.3 billion in a pension fund surplus, would also free up about $650 million in one-shot budget savings.
Although State House watchers have said there appears to be enough support to pass the legislation needed for the bond sale, Littell said he expects it to fail.

"I'm convinced there's more than enough to defeat it," he said. Littell said he is not opposed to Whitman's proposal to reclassify a portion of the pension system's surplus and use it to pay down some of the unfunded liability and for budget savings.

In fact, he said that strategy should be used to avoid the need for bonds entirely, by simply waiting for the pension system's investment strategy to continue building a surplus large enough to wipe out the liability.

Whitman and state Treasurer Brian Clymer have said turning the unfunded liability into a bond debt would capitalize on the current low interest rate environment and dramatically reduce the long-term payments required to pay off the debt.
Clymer also said using up the surplus would be irresponsible, since it is used to protect the pension fund against downturns in investment revenues.
The state last month selected Merrill Lynch & Co to underwrite the taxable bond deal if the Legislature gives its approval.
